source.title: When Currencies Break
source.summary: Currency crises in Turkey, Pakistan, Egypt, Iran, and Lebanon. The dollar creates vulnerability, but governance determines the outcome.
source.author: Islamic Economics
source.body_text: Turkey's crisis was Erdogan overriding central bank independence. Pakistan's reflects institutional failure across the board. Egypt's is structural economic narrowness. Iran's combines sanctions with internal dysfunction. Lebanon's is elite capture of the entire banking system. Each case gets specific, fair treatment, with no heroes and no villains. The common thread: the dollar system creates vulnerability for peripheral economies, but domestic governance determines whether that vulnerability becomes a crisis. The same external pressures produce very different outcomes depending on how countries are governed.
